# COBOL Arithmetic, Rounding & Intermediate Precision Specification (#4712)

Part of the **cobolrt-as-a-product** epic ([#4710](https://github.com/squid-protocol/gitgalaxy/issues/4710)).
Single source of truth: [`gitgalaxy/standards/cobol/arith.py`](../../gitgalaxy/standards/cobol/arith.py).
Generated by `python -m gitgalaxy.standards.cobol regen`.

Reference: **IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC26-4940-06)**
Chapters: *Arithmetic statements*, *Common phrases and concepts for arithmetic statements*,
*DIVIDE statement*, *COMPUTE statement*.

| Rule ID | Status | Title | IBM Manual Reference | Register |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `RT-CBL-DECIMAL-CONSTANT-SCALE` | `DIFFERS` | A numeric literal in a decimal expression is libcob's decimal constant: an ADD / SUBTRACT raises its scale and an exponent trims it in place, and later uses of the same literal see the change; a program restart resets it | GnuCOBOL dc_N decimal constant caching behavior | `C2` |
| `RT-CBL-DIVIDE-IN-FUNCTION-ARGUMENT` | `MATCHED` | A division inside an intrinsic function's argument (cob_intr_binop): a zero divisor gives 0 with the size error raised, never NaN | cobol-lr: Intrinsic functions | - |
| `RT-CBL-DIVIDE-INTERMEDIATE` | `MATCHED` | An intermediate quotient as cob_decimal_div forms it: scale a.scale - b.scale, the dividend shifted 38 digits more, truncated (38 + max(scale, 0) decimal places) | cobol-lr: Intermediate results in arithmetic statements | - |
| `RT-CBL-DIVIDE-REMAINDER` | `MATCHED` | DIVIDE ... REMAINDER: dividend less divisor times the quotient truncated to the first GIVING receiver's scale (not to its high-order digits); a NaN quotient leaves the remainder receiver unchanged | cobol-lr: DIVIDE statement: REMAINDER phrase | - |
| `RT-CBL-EXPONENTIATION` | `MATCHED` | a ** b as cob_decimal_pow: a whole exponent exactly, else through double; 0 ** 0 is 1 with the size error raised, a non-finite result NaN with the size error raised | cobol-lr: Arithmetic expressions: Exponentiation | - |
| `RT-CBL-OSVS-INTERMEDIATE-ALIGN` | `MATCHED` | ARITHMETIC-OSVS: an intermediate truncated to the statement's decimal places as cob_decimal_align does it (fewer places than the scale lose as many low-order digits: 579 aligned to 2 places is 500) | cobol-pg: ARITH(COMPAT|EXTEND) | `C2` |
| `RT-CBL-SIZE-ERROR` | `MATCHED` | ON SIZE ERROR: the receiver unchanged, and the condition true, when the value does not fit or is NaN | cobol-lr: Common phrases: SIZE ERROR | - |
| `RT-CBL-STORE-RESULT` | `MATCHED` | An arithmetic result stored: low-order digits past the scale dropped or ROUNDED (half away from zero), high-order digits past the PICTURE (or the bytes, TRUNC(BIN) / COMP-5) lost; the typed-layer readers return exactly what the store leaves | cobol-lr: ROUNDED phrase | - |
| `RT-CBL-UNSIGNED-BINARY-ABSOLUTE` | `MATCHED` | ADD / SUBTRACT into an unsigned binary item where cobc compiles native arithmetic: the receiver takes the absolute value (1 - 3 is 2), as IBM; the oracle wraps (declared) | cobol-lr: ADD and SUBTRACT statements | `C4` |
| `RT-CBL-ZERO-DIVISOR-NAN` | `MATCHED` | A zero divisor raises the size error and makes the intermediate libcob's NaN: NaN in, NaN out through + - * and unary minus, and a store of NaN leaves the receiver unchanged | cobol-lr: DIVIDE statement | `C14` |

## 2. Rounding Modes (IBM Enterprise COBOL ROUNDED / ROUNDED MODE IS ...)

| ID | Mode Name | Java RoundingMode | IBM Syntax Clause | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | `TRUNCATION` | `DOWN` | ROUNDED MODE IS TRUNCATION (or omitted ROUNDED phrase) | Truncation toward zero; excess fractional digits are dropped. |
| `1` | `NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO` | `HALF_UP` | ROUNDED (default) or ROUNDED MODE IS NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO | Round half away from zero (COBOL default ROUNDED phrase). |
| `2` | `NEAREST-EVEN` | `HALF_EVEN` | ROUNDED MODE IS NEAREST-EVEN | Round half to nearest even digit (banker's rounding). |
| `3` | `NEAREST-TOWARD-ZERO` | `HALF_DOWN` | ROUNDED MODE IS NEAREST-TOWARD-ZERO | Round half toward zero. |
| `4` | `TOWARD-GREATER` | `CEILING` | ROUNDED MODE IS TOWARD-GREATER | Round toward positive infinity. |
| `5` | `TOWARD-LESSER` | `FLOOR` | ROUNDED MODE IS TOWARD-LESSER | Round toward negative infinity. |
| `6` | `PROHIBITED` | `UNNECESSARY` | ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED | No rounding permitted; if non-zero fractional digits are lost, ON SIZE ERROR is raised. |

## 3. Size Error Conditions (ON SIZE ERROR Phrase)

| Condition | Trigger Event | Receiver Action | Governed By Rule | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` | Divisor evaluates to zero in DIVIDE or REMAINDER | Receiver unchanged; intermediate set to NaN | `RT-CBL-ZERO-DIVISOR-NAN` | A zero divisor raises size error and makes intermediate NaN, leaving receiver unchanged. |
| `OVERFLOW_INTEGER_DIGITS` | Magnitude of result exceeds PICTURE integer digits capacity | Receiver unchanged | `RT-CBL-SIZE-ERROR` | When result does not fit integer digits, receiver is untouched and size error raised. |
| `EXPONENTIATION_ZERO_POW_ZERO` | Base is zero and exponent is zero (0 ** 0) | Result yields 1; size error raised | `RT-CBL-EXPONENTIATION` | 0 ** 0 yields 1 with the size error raised under standard COBOL rules. |
| `EXPONENTIATION_NON_FINITE` | Negative base with non-integer power or overflow to infinity | Result yields NaN; size error raised | `RT-CBL-EXPONENTIATION` | Non-finite exponentiation results raise size error and yield NaN intermediate. |
| `PROHIBITED_ROUNDING_TRUNCATION` | ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED and non-zero fractional digits would be dropped | Receiver unchanged | `RT-CBL-SIZE-ERROR` | Truncating non-zero digits under MODE PROHIBITED triggers size error. |

## 4. Intermediate Precision & Scaling Specifications

- **Division Intermediate Quotient Scale Formula:**
  `scale = 38 + max(scaleA - scaleB, 0)` with `RoundingMode.DOWN`.
- **DIVIDE ... REMAINDER Formula:**
  `Remainder = Dividend - (Quotient_truncated_to_giving_scale * Divisor)`.
- **NaN Scale Marker:** `-32768` (`Cobol.NAN_SCALE` / libcob `COB_DECIMAL_NAN`).
- **Unsigned Binary Native Arithmetic Rule:** Absolute value taken under IBM Enterprise COBOL semantics.
